title: End-to-End Compliance Evidence Blueprint for Model Serving Incidents
author: Sasha Patel
body:
Overview
--------
This blueprint defines a reproducible, auditable process for collecting, preserving, and delivering compliance evidence when a model-serving security incident (for example: data exposure, unauthorized inference access, or pipeline compromise) is suspected or confirmed. It ties together RBAC/auth telemetry, audit logs, data residency constraints, secure SDLC artifacts, incident response actions, and exception governance so that evidence can be produced quickly for investigations and regulators while minimizing attack surface and legal risk.

Scope and intent
----------------
- Scope: model-serving infra across Redwood Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments (VPC / on‑prem).
- Intent: provide a single reference for on-call, SRE, security, and compliance teams to preserve an evidentiary record that satisfies internal SLAs and common regulatory requirements (GDPR, SOC-type audits, and contractual data residency constraints).

Key objectives
--------------
1. Minimize time-to-preservation (target: evidence-preserved within 60 minutes of incident identification).
2. Ensure chain-of-custody metadata for all artifacts.
3. Respect data residency and retention policies during evidence handling.
4. Provide a defensible, repeatable packaging format for audit teams and regulators.
5. Define exception and risk-acceptance workflows for constrained environments.

Ownership and contact matrix
---------------------------
- Primary owner: Security Incident Response (security).
- Secondary owners: Eng-SRE (ops), Eng-Serving-Runtime (runtime artifacts), Legal (privacy/regulatory).
- Pager escalation: security-oncall -> incident commander -> CISO (per oncall rota).

Roles and responsibilities (short)
- Incident Responder: initiates preservation, documents chain-of-custody, and coordinates packaging.
- SRE: executes log/metric exports, snapshotting caches, and instance images if required.
- Runtime Engineer: extracts model artifacts, model hashes, and inference cache manifests.
- Legal & Privacy: validates cross-border steps and approves evidence exports where required.

Evidence taxonomy (what to collect)
----------------------------------
- Authentication & Authorization:
  - RBAC change logs (role grants/revocations) with timestamp and actor ID.
  - Token issuance/rotation events (service identity issuance, X.509 events).
- Audit logging:
  - API gateway request logs (request id, client id, route, timestamp, latency, response code).
  - Inference-level logs (minimal prompt/response metadata; NEVER include full customer plaintext prompts unless legal-approved).
  - System-level logs: kube-audit, kubelet, node syslog, cloud-control-plane events where available.
- Model & artifact metadata:
  - Model manifest (model id, version, SHA256 hash, quantization profile).
  - Container image digests and deployment manifests (k8s manifests, Helm values).
- State snapshots:
  - KV cache snapshot (only metadata and cache keys; raw cached customer data requires Legal signoff).
  - Process/thread dumps and core files (if crash is relevant).
- Network & storage traces:
  - Flow logs, VPC/Security Group ACLs at incident window, s3 access logs for relevant objects.
- Identity correlation artifacts:
  - Authentication traces linking user/service identity to requests (session ids, client certs, exchange traces).

Retention and residency rules (guidelines)
-----------------------------------------
- Default evidence retention: 2 years for audit copies, 90 days for hot evidence before cold archival.
- Data residency enforcement: evidence that includes customer data must remain in the originating region unless Legal provides an export authorization.
- Redaction: when evidence contains PII or customer-provided content, redact according to the Data Masking Standard (see related page).

Chain-of-custody manifest (required fields)
------------------------------------------
Each packaged evidence bundle MUST include a plain-text manifest with these top-level fields (one per line):
- incident_id: unique RFC4122 UUID assigned by incident commander
- collected_by: person or service (email)
- collection_time_utc: RFC3339 timestamp
- artifact_list: newline-separated list of artifact filenames included in the bundle
- origin_region: AWS/GCP/Azure region or "on-prem"
- legal_approval: boolean (true/false) and approver name if applicable
- handling_notes: free text field for special handling steps or redaction summary

Example manifest snippet (plain text)
-----------------------------------
incident_id: 2f7e1b9c-4b25-4b6b-9f1a-0a6f4e5c9a11
collected_by: sasha.patel@redwood.ai
collection_time_utc: 2026-12-08T18:42:12Z
artifact_list:
  - authz_roles_2026-12-08.log
  - api_gw_requests_2026-12-08.csv
  - model-manifest-v3.json
origin_region: eu-west-1
legal_approval: true (Priya Nair)
handling_notes: redacted user prompts per legal guidance; cache snapshot trimmed to keys only

Preservation runbook (step-by-step)
----------------------------------
1) Triage and scope: Incident Responder captures initial incident id and brief summary in the incident channel.
2) Preservation trigger: If the incident involves suspected data exposure, run the preservation playbook and mark evidence_hot = true.
3) Short-term snapshot (within 60 minutes):
   - SRE: export API gateway logs for incident window:
     curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $EXPORT_TOKEN" "https://logs.redwood.internal/api/v1/export?from=2026-12-08T18:30:00Z&to=2026-12-08T19:00:00Z&app=api-gateway" > api_gw_requests.csv
   - Runtime: capture model manifest and container image digest:
     kubectl -n model-serving get deploy model-foo -o jsonpath='{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}' > image_digest.txt
   - SRE: snapshot k8s events and kube-audit for affected namespace: kubectl get events -n model-serving --since=1h -o yaml > k8s-events.yaml
4) Secure packaging: write manifest, compress artifacts to encrypted archive (AES-256) and store in evidence bucket with restricted ACLs. Example:
   tar czf - api_gw_requests.csv model-manifest-v3.json k8s-events.yaml | gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 -o incident-2f7e1b9c-20261208.tgz.gpg
   gsutil cp incident-2f7e1b9c-20261208.tgz.gpg gs://evidence-prod/eu-west-1/incident-2f7e1b9c/
5) Notify Legal & Privacy for cross-border approval if evidence leaves region.
6) Handoff: update incident tracker with storage path, manifest digest (SHA256), and responsible custodian.

Packaging format and delivery
----------------------------
- Standard bundle naming: incident-<incident_id>-<region>-<YYYYMMDD>.tgz.gpg
- Include checksums: SHA256 manifest and artifact-level checksums.
- Only share decrypted content with Legal/Compliance or external auditors through recorded, access-controlled sessions (e.g., ephemeral session to a dedicated review VM).

Exception and risk-acceptance flow
--------------------------------
Situations may require deviation (for example, on-prem customers disallow remote snapshot export). Follow this flow:
1. Document exception request in the Exception Tracker with justification and risk assessment.
2. Engineer proposes mitigations (on-site retention, remote audit under supervision, data minimization).
3. Security + Legal review and approve/deny. Approval must include a timebound limit and required evidence handling steps.

Integration with secure SDLC and deployments
------------------------------------------
- CI/CD must emit immutable build artifacts and store image digests in the Artifact Registry (artifact->SHA mapping). This allows matching runtime images to source commits during an investigation.
- Pre-deployment: include a "forensics hook" in release templates that records the deployment manifest to the artifact registry with an immutable timestamp.
- Post-deployment testing: smoke tests must capture route-level access logs and synthetic requests that will help determine baseline behavior when investigating anomalies.

Audit and verification (what auditors will look for)
-------------------------------------------------
Auditors commonly validate:
- Evidence completeness and timestamps for the incident window.
- Chain-of-custody and manifest integrity (checksums match).
- Residency compliance (evidence did not cross restricted boundaries without approval).
- RBAC changes correlating to the incident (who granted what, when).

Checklist for release with evidence considerations
------------------------------------------------
- Build artifact stored with checksum: yes/no
- RBAC change docs for the release: yes/no
- K8s manifests and Helm values archived: yes/no
- Canary traffic logs available for the release window: yes/no
- Evidence hooks validated in CI: yes/no

Example forensic queries (search patterns)
----------------------------------------
- Locate all requests tied to a principal in a 15-minute window (Elasticsearch):
  GET /_search?q=client_id:svc-account-123 AND @timestamp:[2026-12-08T18:30:00Z TO 2026-12-08T18:45:00Z]&size=10000
- Find RBAC grant events for a user:
  SELECT * FROM authz_events WHERE event_type = 'role_grant' AND target_user = 'alice@acme.com' AND ts > '2026-12-01' ORDER BY ts DESC;

Privacy & redaction notes
------------------------
- Do not include plaintext customer inputs or direct model outputs unless specifically required and approved by Legal. When approved, redact per the Redaction Matrix and record the redaction rationale in handling_notes.
- When evidence includes PII, mark the bundle as "sensitive" and apply additional ACLs and retention limits.

Post-incident evidence lifecycle
-------------------------------
- Day 0–7: Hot evidence retained with restricted access for active investigation.
- Day 8–90: Cold storage in evidence-bucket with logged, but limited, access.
- >90 days: Archive to long-term immutable store (WORM) if required by regulator; otherwise schedule secure deletion per retention schedule.

Training and drills
------------------
- Conduct an annual evidence preservation drill (game-day) that includes cross-team coordination: SRE, Runtime, Security, Legal.
- Maintain a one-page quick reference at /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/evidence-quick-reference for oncall responders.

Appendix A — Quick export commands (examples)
-------------------------------------------
- Export S3 object list for prefix and copy to evidence bucket (awscli):
  aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket customer-logs --prefix "prod/model-foo/2026-12-08/" --query 'Contents[].{Key:Key,LastModified:LastModified}' > s3-list.json
  aws s3 cp s3://customer-logs/prod/model-foo/2026-12-08/api.log .
- Create encrypted archive locally and upload:
  tar czf - api_gw_requests.csv model-manifest-v3.json | gpg --symmetric --cipher-algo AES256 -o /tmp/incident.tgz.gpg
  aws s3 cp /tmp/incident.tgz.gpg s3://evidence-prod/eu-west-1/incident-2f7e1b9c/

Appendix B — Minimal artifact naming conventions
-----------------------------------------------
- <service>-<artifact>-<YYYYMMDD>-<HHMMSS>.<ext> (e.g., api-gw-requests-20261208-184212.csv)
